# CoLa2+EarthRanger

This tutorial generates a species distribution model (SDM) using CoLa new modules. You will use EarthRanger API (via ecoscope Python package)

### 1. Obtain points from EarthRanger

Access and download points from EarthRanger server, using ecoscope Python package.

```{r earthranger, opts.label=}
library(cola)

# (wd <- file.path(Sys.getenv('COLA_DATA_PATH'), sessionIDgen(folder = TRUE)))
(wd <- 'C:/Cola/sessions/demo')
dir.create(wd, showWarnings = FALSE)

erPoints <- file.path(wd, 'points_2024-2025.shp')
erRaster <- file.path(wd, 'raster_2024-2025.tif')
```

```{r earthranger, opts.label=}
# Run if file doesn't exists
if (!file.exists(erPoints)){
  ERpoints <- cola::earthRanger_py(
      server = 'https://twiga.pamdas.org', 
      username = 'IGonzalez', 
      pwd = 'temp12345',
      datefrom = '2024-01-01',
      dateto = '2025-12-31',
      subject = 'NAM_test',
      outshp = erPoints, 
      outtif = erRaster,
      dokde = 1,
      spatresinmeters = 10000)
}
```


### 2. Plot the downlodaded layers

```{r earthrangerplot}
library(terra)

# rastLayer <- rast( erRaster )
# plot(rastLayer, main = 'KDE')

vectLayer <- vect( erPoints )
dim(vectLayer)
plot(vectLayer, main = 'Earth Ranger points')

# Check year values
range(vectLayer$year)
```


### 3. Start CoLa2

You need to set up an GEE account before using CoLa2. Then is necessary to initialize your user account locally. Run the following R command to obtain instructions. Place your GEE account/project name as argument for `ee.Authenticate(YOUR_USER)`. This is required to run just once right after CoLa2 installation and before the first attempt to connect GEE

```{r upload}
cola::initialize_cola_ee(py = Sys.getenv("ER_PYTHON_PATH"))
```

This should authenticate you inside CoLa-GEE python streamflow.


### 4. Upload the layer to GEE
We dont't have absences yet, so we will ask the script to simulate the same ampunt of background points (spatial random) as the downloaded from EarthRanger.

```{r upload}
cola2Upl <- cola::localPoints2ee_py(
    ee_project = 'gonzalezivan',
    point_path = erPoints,
    ee_layer = 'projects/gonzalezivan/assets/demo/er_points_2024_2025',
    presence_col = NULL, # We dont have. CoLa2 creates 'preabs' automatically
    num_abs = nrow(vectLayer))
```

You can visit: `https://code.earthengine.google.com/#` to check the progress in the upload task. Usually takes few minutes.

### 5. Extract pixel values

Collect the imagery pixel values at the points locations. This operations creates a table with `r` rows, and `b` columns, `r` x `b`. `r` is number of records and `b` is number of bands. This task 

```{r extract}
cola2Ext <- cola::sdm_extract_py(
  ee_project = 'gonzalezivan',
  occurrence_asset = 'projects/gonzalezivan/assets/demo/er_points_2024_2025',
  gee_assets = 'projects/gonzalezivan/assets/demo', # Saving results here
  species = 'species1',
  model_id = 'model1',
  batch_size = 5000, 
  batch_year = min(range(vectLayer$year)),
  working_dir = wd, # Local folder 
  max_concurrent = 5, # Number of tiles to be executed simultanously
  column_train = "preabs",
  predictor_source = "modis"
  )
```


### 6. Train the model

Train the model by identifying which variables separates better the presences (1) and absences (0) in your dataset.

```{r fitting}
cola2Fit <- cola::sdm_model_fitting_py(
  ee_project = 'gonzalezivan',
  gee_assets = 'projects/gonzalezivan/assets/demo', # Saving results here
  species = 'species1',
  model_id = 'model1',
  modex = 'binary',
  target_col = "preabs",
  predictor_source = "modis",
  
  working_dir = wd, # Local folder 
  local_csv = file.path(wd, 'ee_training.csv'),
  
  imp_thresh = 0.2,
  categorical_threshold = 10,
  )
```

```{r prediction}
cola::sdm_prediction_py(predictor_source, …)
```

```{r download}
cola::export_ee2gd_py(username, …)
```




## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
